result.rationale: The diff verifiably removes the office365calendar console.error block ('Outlook error grabbing new tokens ~ zodError:', tokenResponse.error, 'MS response:', responseJson) and replaces schema.safeParse with parseRefreshTokenResponse, which throws the generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' with no logging of the zod issue or provider response. This is a real, specific loss of debuggability for token-refresh failures, but not incorrect behavior — an observability concern relevant to maintainers, hence important_non_bug.

judged_text: The removed console.error block means a failed token parse now surfaces only the context-free 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' with neither the zod issue nor the Microsoft response logged. When the new minimum-schema or provider-schema parse rejects a real Microsoft response, on-call debugging has no record of what the provider returned, misdirecting investigation of Outlook token failures introduced by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the prior `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens...", tokenResponse.error, "MS response:", responseJson)` block was removed when switching from `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`. The new helper (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) throws a generic `Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure and does not log the Zod error details or the provider response. This is a diff-grounded observability/debuggability regression rather than a functional defect.
